newsitem.title: BULGARIA: World Bank's IFC to help finance Sofia Hilton hotel.
newsitem.headline: World Bank's IFC to help finance Sofia Hilton hotel.

text.p: Bulgaria will build a Hilton hotel in the capital Sofia at a cost of $46.7 million, of which the World Bank's International Finance Corporation (IFC) will provide and arrange $20.3 million in loans, officials said on Tuesday.

The IFC, the World Bank's private sector finance arm, will make a $10.8 million direct loan and a $9.5 million loan syndicated among banks from Germany, Austria, France and the Netherlands, the first of its kind for Bulgaria.
"We very much hope that by doing a few visible showcase transactions we can set an example for other investors," said Harold Rosen, the IFC's director for South and Central Europe.
"A transaction like that with real private sector character to it and good long term viability is a very important thing for Bulgaria to see at the present moment."

Khosrow Zamani, division manager of the IFC's Europe 1 Division, said France's Feal International SA will take a 40 percent stake in the project, Ladbroke Group Plc unit Hilton International 20 percent, Sofia municipality 22 percent and Bulgarian construction company Glavbulgarstroy 18 percent.
He said the 256-room five-star hotel would be managed by Hilton International.

Deputy Prime Minister Evgeni Bakardzhiev said earlier this month construction on the site beside Sofia's National Palace of Culture was expected to start in September. Previous plans for a Hilton hotel in the city never got off the ground. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
